questions.question: Distinguish between physical and chemical refining processes, giving one example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Physical processes separate substances using physical properties without forming new substances (e.g. magnetic separation, froth flotation, panning, dissolving and evaporating salt). Chemical processes form new substances to release the metal from its compound (e.g. smelting iron ore with carbon; electrolysis of aluminium oxide; dissolving gold in cyanide).

questions.question: Describe how iron was smelted in southern Africa in the Iron Age.
questions.expected_answer: Iron ore (haematite or magnetite) was broken up and charcoal made from wood; layers of charcoal and ore were loaded into a clay furnace; goatskin bellows blew air through clay tuyères to make the charcoal burn at about 1 200 °C; carbon monoxide from the charcoal removed oxygen from the iron oxide; a spongy bloom of iron and slag formed, which smiths reheated and hammered to remove slag and forge tools such as hoes and spears.

questions.question: Write the balanced equation for the reduction of haematite in a blast furnace, explain the role of limestone, and explain how pig iron is turned into steel.
questions.expected_answer: Fe2O3 + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO2. Limestone decomposes to calcium oxide (CaCO3 → CaO + CO2), which reacts with sand impurities to form slag (CaO + SiO2 → CaSiO3) that floats on the iron and is removed. Pig iron (about 4% carbon, brittle) has oxygen blown through it in a basic oxygen furnace to burn off most of the carbon, giving steel with less than about 1% carbon, which is strong and tough.
